title: Preflight probe
description: One preflight probe executed as a task DAG node under the `preflight-v1` runner (ADR-CHK-0001). A probe observes one fact about the host, the checkout, or a remote and compares it with `expected`. Its `class` decides the outcome of a mismatch: an `extrinsic` probe observes something outside the candidate (an environment variable, a registry, a credential, a toolchain version, the fetched base), so its failure yields `blocked`, marks every dependent blocked-environment, and is never written to the result cache, because it says nothing about the candidate; an `intrinsic` probe observes the candidate itself (a tracked file, a clean tree, a command over the checkout), so its failure yields `fail` and is cached like any other observation. The same probe list runs locally and in the pull-request lane from the same descriptor, so the planned node sets are byte-identical for the same base and candidate.

probe_id.description: Probe identity, unique within one descriptor node. Lower-case, starts with a letter, hyphenated.

probe_class.description: `extrinsic`: the observed fact lives outside the candidate; a mismatch yields `blocked` and is never cached. `intrinsic`: the observed fact is the candidate itself; a mismatch yields `fail` and is cached.

probe_status.description: `pass`: observed matches expected. `fail`: an intrinsic mismatch, cached as a real observation. `blocked`: an extrinsic mismatch or an observation that could not be made at all; never cached, re-executed on every plan, and every dependent is blocked-environment. `skipped`: a probe in `depends_on` did not pass, so this probe did not execute and `observed` is null.

environment_probe.description: Reads one environment variable of the executing host.

name.description: The variable name. Its value is compared with `expected` when given; otherwise presence is the observation.

expected.description: The exact value required. Absent means the variable only has to be set.

file_probe.description: Inspects one file resolved inside the checkout.

path.description: Repository-relative path. Paths escaping the checkout are refused before execution.

expected_sha256.description: The digest the file content must carry. Absent means only existence is observed.

must_exist.description: True when absence is a mismatch; false when the probe asserts absence.

command_probe.description: Runs one declared argument vector with `shell: false` and observes its exit status.

argv.description: Argument vector under the same rules as a task node: a bare executable name first, never a shell string.

expected_exit.description: The exit status that counts as a match.

check.description: `base-up-to-date`: the candidate contains the freshly fetched `base`. `clean-tree`: no tracked or untracked change is pending. `commit-range`: every commit from `base` to the candidate satisfies the commit grammar.

base.description: The base reference or exact commit for `base-up-to-date` and `commit-range`.

registry_probe.description: Reaches one package registry or remote endpoint.

url.description: The endpoint to reach. An unreachable host is `blocked`, never `fail`.

expected_version.description: The version the registry must report for the package the URL names. Absent means reachability is the observation.

toolchain_probe.description: Compares the observed runtime versions with the adopter toolchain manifest (ADR-CHK-0002).

manifest_path.description: Repository-relative path of the manifest that conforms to toolchain-manifest.schema.json.

credential_probe.description: Confirms a credential named by the credential manifest (ADR-SEC-0001) is present without reading its value into any report.

manifest_id.description: The manifest entry identity. The observed value of a credential probe is always redacted.

probe.description: The observation to make, closed per `kind`.

expected.description: Human-readable statement of the expected observation, printed beside `observed` in the runner report.

observed.description: The redacted observation. Null before execution and for a `skipped` probe. A value that resembles a secret is replaced by a fixed marker before it reaches any report or diagnostics path; a `credential` probe never carries the raw value.

remediation.description: What the operator does when the probe does not pass, printed with the outcome.

depends_on.description: Probe ids in the same node that must pass first. A probe whose dependency is `blocked` is blocked-environment; one whose dependency is `fail` or `skipped` is `skipped`.

examples.remediation: Run git fetch origin main and merge or rebase the candidate onto it.
Install the node version declared in .devai/config/toolchain.json.
Provide the credential named npm-publish in the credential manifest.
